Ambitious Impact published one public model of this charity's work, in January 2021.

| Model | By | Date | Years of healthy life per $1,000 | Cells reproduced |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [CEARCH: exploratory cause-prioritisation research (Ambitious Impact, 2021 idea report)](/cearch) | AIM | January 2021 | <span data-figure="headline" data-model="cearch-aim">44</span> | 27 |

**Purely theoretical.** Ambitious Impact's estimate is of the idea, written before CEARCH existed, not of the charity's own results. It is shown because CEARCH runs the programme today ([checked October 2026](https://exploratory-altruism.org/)) and no model of its actual work exists yet.

**Where we differ from Ambitious Impact.** CEARCH works through the money it moves or redirects, not a programme of its own, so our view values each such dollar the way the site values every meta charity's: by GiveWell's Top Charities, each at its live result on this site (where its money goes: its work is in global health and poverty), so the sliders move it too. A new organisation's chance of success is the site's shared 56%, taken as an expected value over success and failure (a failed organisation still moves 20% of the money and spends for three years), the same step for every new meta organisation. Ambitious Impact's own valuation stays in the evaluator view. [How money moved is valued](https://github.com/heychristoph/charityevals/blob/main/docs/normalization.md#28-money-moved-success-and-career-changes-one-method-october-2026).
